claude.sample_unit: clinician-annotated hypokalemia cases (each run in triplicate)

links.outcome: Rate of appropriate potassium dosing recommendations versus clinician answers
links.effect: Without dosing guidance, average accuracy 45% and 165 total errors; with guidance accuracy 65% and 104 errors. Dosing and concurrent interventions had the highest error rates.
links.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.

links.effect: GPT-5-Chat conveyed high confidence for 100% of responses despite 45-65% accuracy.
links.quote: GPT-5-Chat conveyed a high level of confidence for 100% of responses, while labeling 80% and 76% of cases as highly complex with and without the criteria, respectively.

links.outcome: Accuracy and errors with versus without clinician-curated dosing guideline provided to model
links.effect: Total errors dropped from 165 to 104; accuracy improved from 45% to 65%; severity of potential harm reduced with guidance, though still considerable.
links.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.

links.outcome: Whether the existing agentic benchmark reflects clinical complexity of potassium dosing
links.effect: Model showed unfit performance on a comprehensive potassium replacement task despite a benchmark using a single dosing rule; accuracy 45-65%.
links.quote: GPT-5-Chat assessment on a comprehensive medication management task for potassium replacement showed improvement with dosing guidance, yet unfit benchmarking performance.

links.effect: With the dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65%.
links.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.

links.effect: Total errors were 165 without guidance and 104 with guidance; concurrent-intervention and dosing recommendations had the highest error rates.
links.quote: Recommendations on concurrent interventions and dosing had the highest rate of errors in both groups.

links.effect: GPT-5-Chat gave high confidence for 100% of responses despite average accuracy of 45% without and 65% with criteria.
links.quote: GPT-5-Chat conveyed a high level of confidence for 100% of responses, while labeling 80% and 76% of cases as highly complex with and without the criteria, respectively.

links.outcome: Dosing recommendation accuracy and total errors
links.effect: Total errors dropped from 165 to 104 and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with the dosing guideline.
links.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.

links.outcome: Model confidence calibration on complex clinical cases
links.effect: GPT-5-Chat conveyed high confidence for 100% of responses despite accuracy being only 45% to 65%.
links.quote: GPT-5-Chat conveyed a high level of confidence for 100% of responses, while labeling 80% and 76% of cases as highly complex with and without the criteria, respectively.

links.outcome: Potential harm severity and dosing error rate
links.effect: Potential harm scores were considerable in both groups, with recommendations on concurrent interventions and dosing having the highest error rate.
links.quote: Potential harm scores were considerable in both groups, however, a notable reduction in severity scores occurred with the dosing guidance document.
